newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech floods move downstream, rains recede.
newsitem.headline: Czech floods move downstream, rains recede.

text.p: The worst flooding in Czech territory this century struck two major cities on Wednesday and the government released more than one billion crowns ($30.7 million) for rescue operations in stricken regions.
The confirmed death toll rose to nine and dozens of people were reported missing in the floods, touched off by torrential rains last weekend.
But flood tides moved downstream on Wednesday as a gradual return of drier weather restored hope in hard-hit areas.
Environment Minister Jiri Skalicky said the flood damage was enormous and would exceed 10 billion crowns.
CTK news agency said more than 16,000 people near the third largest city, Ostrava, were evacuated when a dam on the Ostravice river had to open its gates to avoid bursting.
Parts of Ostrava, a city of 326,000, were inundated on Wednesday morning.
The surging Morava river swamped Olomouc, a city of 100,000, forcing the main flood control commission to evacuate its headquarters.

A flood wave moved eastwards down the Morava river, which flows from the northeastern corner of the Czech Republic to its southern border with Austria and Slovakia and feeds into the Danube near the Slovak capital Bratislava.
Parts of Poland, Austria, and Slovakia are struggling with floods from the same heavy weather as well.

The Czech government opened emergency food and fuel reserves and extended army participation in rescue efforts. The military was authorised to summon reservists to operate machinery and help rescue teams.

"Immediate funds to be released are 170 million crowns from the ... Finance Ministry and 150 million from the state environment fund," Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus told a news conference after a cabinet session on the flooding.
He said 200 million crowns would be used to postpone local government debt payments. Another 500 million would be freed from a fund set up from proceeds of privatised land.
Flood relief officials called for more shipments of potable water as more springs were contaminated.
Many industries were forced to stop or scale back production due to the flooding or interruptions of power.
Supplies to Volkswagen AG'S Czech car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s. were cut off, forcing the company in the northwestern city of Mlada Boleslav to stop production of its flagship Felicia car.
Rail and road connections to the area remained interrupted and a number of towns lost power, gas and telephone services.
Defence ministry spokesman Vladimir Lukavsky said 1,810 army personnel were operating in flooded regions with 21 helicopters, a number of floating carriers and heavy trucks.
"We are preparing deployment of further personnel and technology, possibly including floating bridges, according to the situation," he told Reuters.
But the weather started improving.

The environment ministry's flood relief official, Josef Reidinger, said the rain had ceased in Moravia and water levels were starting to recede in the north on the Morava and Opava rivers and smaller tributaries.
Forecasts said rain would abate throughout Wednesday. ($ = 32.62 Czech Crowns)
